A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures and appendices. Appendices A–C are retained, and v2 adds Appendices D–E; the corresponding material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical guarantees and proofs, including in Appendices A–C. Table 1 compares theoretical bounds, and Figure 1 illustrates Corollary 6; neither reports original empirical outcomes.

after.justification: Appendix E reports original MFLA training simulations on synthetic Gaussian data, with test losses in Figure 1b and generalization gaps in Figure 2.

M1.justification: The signed two-layer network, regularized objective and MFLA update in Equations (3.1)–(3.2) are retained. Appendix E supplies an experimental configuration of the existing method, without introducing a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Appendix E adds one synthetic regression setting: 50-dimensional Gaussian inputs with adjustable covariance and quadratic single-index labels y = (x1² − 1)/sqrt(2). v1 contains no empirical dataset evaluations; the added coverage remains narrowly focused.

E2.justification: The new simulations evaluate only MFLA, without comparison algorithms. Table 1 retains the same theoretical comparisons with Tel23, SWON23, NOSW24 and Bac17.

E3.justification: Appendix E introduces protocols using a width-50 ReLU network and squared loss: test loss after 200 iterations, and generalization gap after 3000 iterations. The latter uses 100000 test examples and training sizes of 100, 200 and 500. These are new experimental protocols, not revisions to earlier experiments.

E4.justification: Figures 1b and 2 add controlled sweeps examining how effective dimension and training sample count affect test loss and generalization gap. These numerical sensitivity analyses were absent from v1.

E5.justification: Appendix E newly reports averaging Figure 1b's test losses over five independent runs with different data and initializations for each parameter pair. No confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: v2 adds empirical test-loss and generalization-gap results, showing generally larger errors with greater effective dimension and smaller errors with more training samples. These are limited new findings for one synthetic target; no earlier empirical scores are replaced.

T1.justification: v2 corrects the Gibbs density preceding Equation (2.10) to use J' instead of F_beta', fixes an equality to an inequality in Lemma 12, and weakens Lemma 14's success probability from 1 − 2 exp(-Omega(n)) to 1 − n^(-q), explicitly invoking local Lipschitzness. Appendix D adds a quadratic-teacher construction and entropy bound. The main theorems remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions and conclusion retain the claims of nearly linear effective-dimension sample complexity, potentially exponential computation, and conditional polynomial convergence in the Riemannian setting. The additions do not redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: v2 gives a concrete non-Gaussian example covered by Assumption 1, interprets the new simulations as illustrating effective dimension's role, and adds discussion of a purported nontrivial low-entropy teacher in Appendix D. Existing computational and applicability limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix E adds data-generation and initialization instructions, bias handling, network width, iteration budgets and test-set size. It specifies stepsize 0.1, weight decay 0.01 and temperature 0.001, and provides a reproduction-code URL; these disclosures were absent from v1.

R1.justification: Sections 1 and 1.2 now restrict the cited information-theoretic linear sample threshold to isotropic data, refining the comparison with prior research. The cited-work set is unchanged; WMHC24's preprint-to-conference update is bibliographic only.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording, affiliation and notation edits, expands the explanation of input assumptions, and adds cross-references and Appendices D–E. The main narrative and existing proof organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: The original theoretical heatmap is retained as Figure 1a, enlarged and relocated into a two-panel figure with the new test-loss heatmap. Figure 2 adds generalization-gap curves. Table 1 is unchanged, with only localized layout reflow elsewhere.

improvement.justification: Corrections to the Gibbs-density and concentration statements improve rigor, while the documented simulations provide a limited empirical check of the retained theory. These gains outweigh a localized problem in new Appendix D: it states that the uniform teacher outputs ||x||²/d, then gives output 1 at the unit vector e1, leaving its claimed constant separation unsupported as written. The narrow simulations and flawed example limit the improvement.
